summary: The root قثأ (qthA) primarily refers to the cucumber plant and its fruit. It denotes something that grows quickly and is often associated with a specific type of gourd or melon.

headwords.gloss: The land; the place, abounded with the; species of cucumber called
headwords.def: اقثأت الأَرْضُ , (AZ, S, O,) or اقثأ المَكَانُ , (K,) The land, or the place, abounded with the [ species of cucumber called ] قِثّآء . (AZ, S, O, K.) And اقثأ القَوْمُ The people had abundance of قثّآء . (S, O, K.)

headwords.def: قِثَّآءٌ (S, O, Msb, K) and قُثَّآءٌ , (O, Msb, K,) the former of which, with kesr, in the more common, (Msb, TA,) [ A certain vegetable, ] well-known: (K, TA:) [ a species of cucumber; cucumis sativus β fructu flavo majore: (Delile's Floræ Ægypt. Illustr., no. 928:]) or the [ cucumber called ] خِيَار [q. v.]: (S, O, K:) or a general name for the خِيَار , the عَجُور [q. v.], and the فَقُّوس [or فَقُّوص q. v.]: but some apply the name to a species resembling the خيار : (Msb, TA:) and it is said that it is lighter ( أَخَفُّ ) than the خيار : also that عَجُور signifies large قِثّآء : (TA:) the n. un. is قثّآءة . (S, O, Msb.) قِثَّآءُ الحِمَارِ see voce عَلْقَمٌ .
مَقْثَأَةٌ and مَقْثُؤَةٌ , (S, O, K, TA,) or أَرْضٌ مَقْثَأَةٌ and مَقْثُؤَةٌ , (Msb,) A place, or land, of قثّآء , (S, Msb, K,) where قثّآء are sown and grow. (TA.)
